Label the grid with top row a1, a2, a3 and bottom row b1, b2, b3. Each corner piece has 2 neighbors, so it can always be eaten. Each middle piece has 3 neighbors, so it can be eaten only after at least one of its neighbors is gone.

- a2 is a bad move exactly when it is eaten while a1, a3 and b2 are all still present. That means a2 comes before all of a1, a3, b2 in the order, which has probability 1/4.
- b2 is a bad move exactly when it comes before all of b1, b3, a2, which also has probability 1/4.
- Both cannot happen together, because that would require a2 before b2 and b2 before a2. So the two bad events are disjoint.

The number of bad orders is 720 · (1/4 + 1/4) = 360, so the number of valid orders is 720 − 360 = 360.

ANSWER: 360
